done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `calendarYear` excludes amount-like years only for the narrow `... of`, copula, comparison, currency, and suffix forms. For example, “Show an amount around 2025” matches none of those guards, so `parseNamedTimeWindow` converts 2025 into the full 2025 calendar window, overriding the model/prior period. This directly violates the requirement that an amount is never read as a year. The existing `AMOUNT_MODIFIER` vocabulary should also protect direct amount phrases such as `amount around 2025` and `cost approximately 2025`.
findings.title: Not done: direct approximate amounts are still treated as calendar years

findings.body: The added matrix invokes `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`; that fixture uses a fake LLM, executor/warehouse, audit service, dimensions, reports, and resolver (unchanged lines 1221–1267). The period-control rerun test uses the same fixture. The registered suites remain Node and jsdom/Vitest tests, with no Playwright flow through a running frontend, API, and real database. Therefore the named-period override, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and user-driven period rerun still lack the required end-to-end proof. The successful close run only executed these lower-boundary suites.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
